policy_presence.summary: UC Berkeley distributes AI guidance across OERCS appropriate-use advisory, Academic Senate recommendations, the July 1, 2026 Student Conduct Code, and the 2026 Research Misconduct Policy.

ai_disclosure.summary: Academic Senate guidance provides optional syllabus frameworks for instructors to require tool acknowledgment and prompt descriptions on permitted assignments. Researchers should disclose generative AI use in research reports, manuscripts, and publications where appropriate (specifying tools, scope, and human verification); for grant proposals, researchers should follow applicable funding agency disclosure requirements.

coursework.summary: Coursework use is conditioned on explicit instructor permission in the syllabus; unauthorized use of AI on academic assignments is prohibited by campus guidance and constitutes academic misconduct under Section 102.01.

exams.summary: No universal exam permission or prohibition is established by reviewed policy. AI use on exams requires explicit instructor authorization; unauthorized use of materials or assistance is defined as cheating under Appendix II of the Student Conduct Code. Tool access is not exam permission.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Public Protection Level P1 data may be entered into AI tools. Entering confidential, personal, or proprietary information (including FERPA student records, unpublished research, or P2–P4 data) is generally prohibited, unless specifically permitted under UC enterprise license agreements and approved protection levels. Instructors are advised not to upload student materials to third-party AI tools lacking a university MOU.

academic_integrity.summary: Undergraduate and general student conduct is governed by the Berkeley Campus Code of Student Conduct revised July 1, 2026 (PACAOS 100.00 / Appendix H). Graduate academic misconduct is adjudicated separately under Graduate Division GAMP with early resolution, formal committee hearings, and a 10-day appeal right.

approved_tools.summary: Berkeley licenses tools including ChatGPT Edu, Gemini, Copilot, BearGPT, and Campus AI Sandbox via CalNet authentication, with varying user eligibility, recharge fees, and P1–P3 data levels. Institutional licensing does not establish course or examination permission.

named_ai_services.summary: Berkeley licenses tools including ChatGPT Edu, Gemini, Copilot, BearGPT, and Campus AI Sandbox via CalNet authentication, with varying user eligibility, recharge fees, and P1–P3 data levels. Institutional licensing does not establish course or examination permission.

teaching_guidance.summary: The Academic Senate recommends clear syllabus expectations, notes that AI detectors are unvalidated, and reminds instructors to ensure student computing access for required tools. Turnitin AI writing detection is not enabled for general bCourses use.

research_guidance.summary: Effective January 1, 2026, research misconduct allegations follow standardized assessment, inquiry, and investigation stages. Researchers are responsible for AI-assisted research and should ensure human verification of facts and citations; Library database scraping/training requires license compliance.

security_procurement.summary: UC Berkeley requires unit-procured tools to adhere to approved protection levels and warns against personal liability from unapproved click-through terms. AI pre-screening questions evaluate organizational risk before committee review.
